tagline: Understand your body. Question the myths. Find your way forward.

home.headline: Your body deserves clear answers.
home.subheading: Explore PCOS, hormones and reproductive health through clear explanations, interactive visuals and myth-busting guides.

myths.claim: PCOS is only an ovarian problem.
myths.explanation: PCOS is a complex condition involving reproductive, hormonal and metabolic features.

myths.claim: Everyone with PCOS has ovarian cysts.
myths.explanation: The name can be misleading; not everyone with PCOS has this ultrasound feature.

myths.claim: Only people with larger bodies have PCOS.
PCOS means someone cannot become pregnant.
myths.explanation: Fertility experiences vary; many people with PCOS can conceive, sometimes with support.
Management is individualised; there is no universal cure.

myths.claim: Pads, tampons or menstrual cups cause PCOS.
myths.answer: No established evidence supports this claim
myths.explanation: Menstrual products are not an established cause of PCOS.

myths.claim: A person can diagnose PCOS from symptoms online.
myths.explanation: Symptoms overlap with other conditions and clinical assessment is required.

appointment_prompts: What changes have I noticed, and when did they begin?
How have my cycles changed, if relevant?
What tests or other causes might need consideration?
What are the benefits, risks and alternatives of proposed treatments?
disclaimer: PCOS Unlocked is an educational resource. It does not provide a diagnosis or replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
